report.verdict: A senior backend engineer with a notable ledger project, but little about what she did in her jobs.
write_up: You're a senior backend engineer working on payouts and ledger services. It's common to see a recent job summed up in one line and an earlier job left blank, but that leaves a recruiter guessing about your work.
The ledger-recon project is the strongest part: it names the library, its language and who uses it. That gives us real work to bring into your About.

Start with the Northwind Pay job, then update the headline and About. Add what you did at Kestrel Labs too. Someone hiring for backend payments work could then connect the project to what you did in your jobs.

cards.line: Senior Backend Engineer at Northwind Pay
cards.cannot_tell: The headline repeats your title and employer but leaves out the payouts and ledger work. Put that specialty beside your title.
cards.example: Senior Backend Engineer | Payouts and ledger services | Go
cards.question: Which part of the payouts and ledger work was yours?

cards.line: Passionate engineer with a track record of delivering scalable solutions. I enjoy hard problems and working with great teams.
cards.cannot_tell: “Scalable solutions” could describe almost any engineer. Your ledger-recon library is much more memorable, and it's sitting in Projects.
cards.example: I work on payouts and ledger services. My project ledger-recon is an open-source ledger reconciliation library in Go, used by three payment companies.
cards.question: What part did you play in developing ledger-recon?

cards.line: Worked on payouts and ledger services.
cards.cannot_tell: This names the services but not what you did to them. Someone searching for API design or distributed systems has no such terms to match in this job.
cards.example: Worked on payouts and ledger services, [what you built or changed] for [who uses it].
cards.question: What did you build or change in the payouts and ledger services, and who uses it?

cards.line: The Software Engineer job at Kestrel Labs has no description.
cards.cannot_tell: The title doesn't say what you built or maintained. Terms such as APIs and backend services have nothing to match under this job.
cards.example: [What you built or maintained at Kestrel Labs] for [who used it], using [tools you used].
cards.question: At Kestrel Labs, did you build APIs, maintain services or work on data systems, and who used them?

cards.line: Open-source ledger reconciliation library in Go. 1,200 GitHub stars, used by three payment companies.
cards.cannot_tell: This is the model for the rest: it names the library, the language and its users. A recruiter doesn't have to guess what ledger-recon is.

fit.why: Your headline and current title name senior backend engineering, and your recent work and project both involve ledgers.
fit.level: senior, the Senior Backend Engineer title
fit.note: “Senior Backend Engineer” is in your headline and current title. “Payouts” and “ledger services” are in your current job. “Go” is in your top skills and project, and “ledger reconciliation” is in your project. Recruiters also search for API design, distributed systems and payment processing; those terms aren't on your profile. Add them only if they describe your work: API design and distributed systems could go in the Northwind Pay description, and payment processing could go in your About if it ties your work together. Move ledger services into your headline first.
